headline: 22 on 422, Walker’s pair, and a market that still lays 2.5
dek: Kansas City rushed for 150, passed for 272 net, and held the ball 30:26 in a 22-6 win over the Chargers; Los Angeles rushed for 73 and held it 29:34, and the next kickoff is at Seattle on Sun Oct 25, 7:20 PM CT, NBC, with Seattle laying 2.5.
videoHook: Five-and-oh, 422 yards, 22 points, and Seattle still laying 2.5 — that is the tape Andy Reid takes on the road.
theEdge: ESPN FPI gives Kansas City 52.8 percent to win at Seattle, DraftKings lists Seattle -2.5 on a 42.5 total, and Polymarket sits at 11.2 percent to win the championship and 18.5 percent to win the AFC — a betting underdog the model still leans toward after 22-6.

pressConferences.speaker: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, Ken Walker, and Nick Bolton
pressConferences.title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, Ken Walker & Nick Bolton Postgame Press Conferences - NFL Week 6

storyline.lede: The 2026 Chiefs are 5-0 because the identity run and the complementary defense keep cashing games the scoreboard does not dress up. Against the Chargers, Kansas City posted 22 first downs, 150 rushing yards on 27 attempts, and 272 net passing yards for 422 total, then won 22-6 while converting 3 of 10 third downs and giving the ball away twice.
body: Kenneth Walker III carried the rush line: 19 carries, 128 yards, and two touchdowns inside a team total of 150. Patrick Mahomes was 23-of-30 for 272 yards with a rating of 89.9, zero sacks, and one interception. Los Angeles managed 15 first downs, 73 rushing yards, and 186 net passing yards. Justin Herbert was 22-of-37 with a 63.3 rating. The clock was close — Kansas City 30:26 on 11 drives, Los Angeles 29:34 on 12 — so the separation was explosives and the end zone, not a long possession monopoly.

Do not blend those clocks. The Chargers afternoon was the higher-yardage, lower-scoring version of the same idea Arrowhead Addict has been calling winning ugly, and Arrowhead Pride’s mailbag is right to ask whether 22 points on 422 is a sustainable weekly diet.

The schedule argument starts now. Arrowhead Pride notes the slate gets tougher beginning in Week 7, and the number agrees in a split way: Seattle is laying 2.5 on a 42.5 total while ESPN FPI still has Kansas City at 52.8 percent. National rankings have the club at No. 2. The film says the staff must turn third down and the kicking game into points before Lumen Field asks them to do it on the road.

lastGameReview.label: Week 6 · Sun, Oct 18 · 3:25 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: At Arrowhead, Kansas City led 3-0 on a 44-yard field goal at Q1 11:20, then Kenneth Walker III ran up the middle 33 yards for a touchdown at Q1 7:21. Harrison Butker’s extra point was no good, wide left, so the score was 9-0. Los Angeles answered with a 23-yard field goal at Q1 1:33. Los Angeles kicked a 30-yard field goal at Q3 10:44. Butker’s 30-yard field goal at Q4 3:52 made the final 22-6. Los Angeles did not score a touchdown.

analysis.body: The rush tape is the cleanest part of the offense. Walker’s 33-yard score was an up-the-middle cut with the extra point missed, so a touchdown drive produced six. His other listed rushing scores sit on the leader line — 19 carries, 128 yards, two touchdowns — inside a team rush of 150 on 27 attempts. Emmett Johnson’s line is separate: 3 rushes and 2 catches, 5 touches. Patrick Mahomes added 5 rushes, including a 10-yard gain off the left end in the second quarter and an 8-yard scramble off the right end in the fourth. That is quarterback movement, not a claim that any throw was play-action.

Mahomes’ dropbacks were clean in the pocket count and messy in the finishing. He was 23-of-30, 0 sacks, with 3 quarterback hits recorded against him, 272 yards, and a rating of 89.9. The interception was a short-right throw intended for Andrew Armstrong, taken by C. Hart for a touchback. Xavier Worthy led the receivers with 7 catches for 73 yards. Travis Kelce had 4 catches. Cyrus Allen had 2 catches, including a 23-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Armstrong played a heavy snap count — Arrowhead Addict has the figure at 42 — and finished with 1 catch. The passing game moved the ball. It did not finish enough drives with touchdowns.

Steve Spagnuolo’s unit held Los Angeles to 259 yards and 73 on the ground. Nick Bolton led the tackle sheet with 11, a total Arrowhead Pride ties to a franchise record for games with 10 or more tackles. Jack Cochrane intercepted Herbert on a short-right throw intended for KeAndre Lambert-Smith and returned it 48 yards. L. Sneed forced a fumble on a short-right completion to Lambert-Smith; Drue Tranquill recovered. Chamarri Conner was credited with 1 sack. Kansas City recorded 9 quarterback hits. A separate second-quarter interception by Christian Roland-Wallace was wiped by Ashton Gillotte’s roughing-the-passer penalty and is not a takeaway. Quentin Johnston’s 57-yard catch to the 1 shows the shell can still lose a deep ball; Los Angeles then kicked, they did not punch it in.

The hidden scoreboard is penalties and kicks. Travis Kelce was flagged for an illegal block above the waist on the opening series. Trent Smith’s holding wiped a play. Kingsley Suamataia’s holding wiped another; the play-by-play notes he had returned. Gillotte’s roughing gave Herbert a drive back. Chris Jones was flagged for roughing late. Butker missed the extra point and later missed a 52-yard field goal wide right. A fourth-quarter Kansas City series with K. Tonga reported eligible ended on downs when Walker went left guard to the 1 for no gain. Special teams also had a punt loose ball forced by T. Dye that was reversed and recovered by the Chargers’ C. Murphy. Kansas City’s box still lists two turnovers. One of them is the Hart interception. The other is not a play this wire lets us rename.

takeaways.title: Walker was the points
takeaways.body: Team rush was 150. Walker was 19 carries for 128 and two touchdowns, with 21 touches once his 2 catches are included. The 33-yard score at Q1 7:21 was the explosive, and the missed extra point kept a touchdown drive at six.

takeaways.title: Third down and the tee lagged the yardage
takeaways.body: Kansas City was 3-of-10 on third down and scored 22 on 422 yards. Butker made kicks of 44, 50, and 30, missed the extra point, and missed from 52. That is how a yardage win becomes a one-score-looking cushion that was actually 16 at the end.

takeaways.title: The takeaways have names
takeaways.body: Cochrane is the interceptor on the live Herbert throw. Sneed forced the Lambert-Smith fumble and Tranquill recovered it. Do not move those credits.

whatWorked: Walker’s up-the-middle and perimeter carries, especially the 33-yard touchdown and the 16-yard run in the fourth quarter
Mahomes at 23-of-30 with 0 sacks and 272 net yards, matching the team passing total
Run defense: Los Angeles 73 rushing yards on 22 attempts, with Bolton at 11 tackles
Cochrane’s interception and the Sneed-forced, Tranquill-recovered fumble
whatDidnt: 3-of-10 on third down and a fourth-quarter snap that died at the 1
The missed extra point and the missed 52-yard field goal
Gillotte’s roughing penalty, which erased a Roland-Wallace interception
The 57-yard completion to Johnston, which put Los Angeles on the doorstep before a field goal

currentState.lede: Kansas City is 5-0, ranked No. 2 in the Arrowhead Pride Week 7 sampling, and still priced as a road underdog for Sun Oct 25, 7:20 PM CT. The offense can move the ball. It is not yet turning that movement into a touchdown rate that travels.

workOn.title: Third down has to cash more than 3-of-10
workOn.body: Eleven drives and 422 yards produced 22 points. Against a Seattle team laying 2.5, another 3-of-10 afternoon on the road will hand the game to field position and the 42.5 total.

workOn.title: Finish red-zone and kicking details
workOn.body: A missed extra point and a miss from 52 turned touchdown and long-field chances into a thinner margin. Reid and Bieniemy need a call at the 1 that is not a stuffed left-guard run, and Butker needs the routine points.

workOn.title: Protect the takeaway math
workOn.body: Kansas City’s box lists two turnovers, including Mahomes to Hart. Los Angeles also had two, via Cochrane and Tranquill. A wiped interception from a roughing foul is a discipline fix for Gillotte, not a scheme trophy.

workOn.title: Sort the receiver snaps before the road
workOn.body: Armstrong’s 42 snaps and 1 catch, Worthy’s 7-for-73, and Kelce’s 4 catches are the usage facts. The room has to be a plan, not a snap-count experiment, once Seattle crowds the box against Walker.

thinkAbout.title: Is the ugly win the identity or the ceiling?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Pride’s mailbag asks if the current approach is sustainable. Arrowhead Addict says the club has remastered winning ugly after last year’s 6-11. Both can be true for five games. Week 7 is the test.

thinkAbout.title: Model versus the number
thinkAbout.body: ESPN FPI has Kansas City at 52.8 percent. DraftKings has Seattle -2.5. That split is the honest edge: respect the building, do not pretend the market has already conceded the trip.

thinkAbout.title: How much Gilman, and how much Bolton?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict tracked Alohi Gilman from 90 percent of the defensive snaps in Week 4 to 49 percent in Week 6. Bolton just posted an 11-tackle game. Spagnuolo’s sub package on the road should be a choice, not a drift.

gamePlan.lede: Win the early-down run, steal a third down, and keep the score ahead of a Seattle team the market still favors by 2.5. Kickoff is Sun Oct 25, 7:20 PM CT on NBC at Seattle. No result exists yet.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City brings a 5-0 run-leaning offense — 150 rushing yards and a 23-of-30 quarterback with 0 sacks last time out — into a loud road building where Seattle is laying the number. The Chiefs’ defense just held a division offense to 73 on the ground and 6 points, with a leak on one 57-yard shot. The leverage is Kansas City’s downhill carries versus a home favorite that will want to squeeze third down, where Kansas City was 3-of-10.

keys.title: Make Walker the first-down answer
keys.body: Inside zone and the occasional Mahomes keep keep Seattle’s second level fit-conscious. Team rush has to stay a team number, with Johnson’s 5-touch changeup available so the closer is not asked to be the whole plan.

keys.title: Manufacture third-down completions
keys.body: Mesh and a running-back screen give Mahomes answers that do not require a 40-yard shot. Worthy and Kelce are the separators. Armstrong has to be a route, not just a snap.

keys.title: Two-deep, then a called zone blitz
keys.body: Cover 2 takes away the Johnston-style shot that broke the Chargers tape. A simulated pressure is a call Spagnuolo can dial — show heat, drop a lineman — not a retroactive label on Cochrane’s interception.

keys.title: Bank the points Butker can make
keys.body: A 42.5 total does not require a track meet. It does require the extra point and the makeable field goal. Leave the 52-yard hero kick for a last resort.

script: Open under center with Walker on inside zone and force a light box before any boot.
On a confirmed run look, boot Mahomes to the perimeter with Kelce as the flat option and Worthy clearing.
Third-and-medium: mesh Kelce and a wide receiver, Johnson as the checkdown.
Second-and-long after a sack or a penalty: spacing screen to Walker so the 3 hits from last game do not become a dropback habit.
Defensively, start in Cover 2 on standard downs and rally Bolton to the ball.
Call a zone blitz on a Seattle second-and-medium, with a defensive lineman dropping and the second level rushing — a call, not a story about last week’s takeaways.

nextGame.label: Week 7 · Sun, Oct 25 · 7:20 PM CT
nextGame.note: Kickoff Sun Oct 25, 7:20 PM CT. Seattle -2.5, total 42.5. FPI leans Kansas City at 52.8 percent. No score to invent.

game.label: Sun, Oct 25 · 7:20 PM CT
game.source: ESPN FPI win probability; ESPN / DraftKings spread

spotlight.title: Walker’s 21 touches sat inside a 150-yard team rush
spotlight.body: 19 carries, 128 yards, two touchdowns, plus 2 catches. Johnson was a 5-touch complement, not the same workload. That split is how Bieniemy keeps the downhill plan fresh on the road.

spotlight.title: 422 yards became 22 because the finishing stalled
spotlight.body: Three made field goals, one missed extra point, one missed 52-yard try, and a snap that died at the 1. The yardage was not the problem. The points per drive were.

spotlight.title: Bolton’s 11 and a named takeaway pair
spotlight.body: Cochrane intercepted Herbert. Sneed forced the fumble Tranquill recovered. Conner had the listed sack. Kansas City put 9 hits on the quarterback. Los Angeles still hit one 57-yard completion.

spotlight.title: No. 2 in the rankings, plus-2.5 on the number
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride’s Week 7 roundup has the Chiefs settling at No. 2. DraftKings still has Seattle favored. Polymarket is at 11.2 percent to win the championship and 18.5 percent to win the AFC.

spotlight.title: The soft opening is over
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride’s schedule piece says the road gets harder starting in Week 7. Denver in Week 8 is the next trip after Seattle. This edition is about Lumen Field, not a December hypothetical.

matchups.unit: Chiefs inside run vs. Seattle front
matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III, Creed Humphrey, Eric Bieniemy
matchups.note: 150 team rushing yards and Walker’s 128 are the evidence. The left-guard stuff at the 1 is the warning, not the identity.

matchups.unit: Mahomes’ pocket vs. Seattle pass rush
matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, 0 sacks and 3 hits allowed last game
matchups.note: Zero sacks is real protection. Three hits say it was not a vacuum. Road noise can change the operation without rewriting the Chargers tape.

matchups.chiefs: Cover 2 with Bolton (11 tackles) and a secondary whose Gilman share dropped to 49 percent
matchups.note: Los Angeles was held to 6 points and still completed a 57-yard ball to Johnston. Two-deep is the correction. It is not a guarantee.

matchups.unit: Third-down offense vs. Seattle’s down package
matchups.opponent: A defense playing with a 2.5-point lead in the number
matchups.note: This is the clearest Kansas City leak. Mesh and the screen are the fixes, not a speech about explosives.

matchups.chiefs: Harrison Butker: made 44, 50, and 30; missed PAT and 52
matchups.note: The made kicks won the margin. The misses are why 422 did not look dominant.

matchups.unit: Linebacker depth vs. a long road week
matchups.chiefs: Nick Bolton, plus Aiden Fisher on the practice squad and Cooper McDonald’s practice window
matchups.note: Bolton is the starter who just made the tackle sheet. Fisher and McDonald are roster news, not a declaration that either plays Sunday.

xsandos.title: Walker downhill on early downs
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 at Seattle, Sun Oct 25, 7:20 PM CT, before the defense can set a pass-only menu
xsandos.why: Walker just cut up the middle for a 33-yard touchdown and finished with 128 of Kansas City’s 150 rushing yards — Bieniemy should keep that track as the first answer at Lumen Field.
xsandos.coaching: Humphrey and the interior reach, Walker presses the mesh point and makes one cut. Johnson (5 touches last game) is the changeup, not the starter’s carry count.

xsandos.title: Boot off the run look
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-5 after a Walker carry, Seattle flowing downhill
xsandos.why: Sell the 150-yard rush profile, then move Mahomes — who was not sacked and took 3 hits — to the perimeter where Kelce’s 4 catches become an easy read.
xsandos.coaching: This is a call for Seattle, not a label on last week’s throws. Worthy clears the corner. Kelce sits in the flat. Mahomes keeps a run option if the end crashes.

xsandos.title: Mesh on third-and-medium
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 to 3rd-and-7, the down Kansas City hit on 3 of 10 against Los Angeles
xsandos.why: Worthy (7 for 73) and Kelce are the rub winners; Armstrong’s 42 snaps have to produce a route, not another interception target with no catch.
xsandos.coaching: Crossers at depth, a sit behind them, Johnson as the outlet. Mahomes throws the first open window. No hero shot required on a 42.5 total.

xsandos.title: Walker screen when the rush declares
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-long after a penalty or a negative play, pass rush climbing up the pocket
xsandos.why: Mahomes took 0 sacks and 3 hits. A screen lets Walker’s 2 catches punish a rush that overplays the 23-of-30 dropback.
xsandos.coaching: Line leads in space. Worthy and a slot hold the edges. Walker catches on the move and gets vertical. Do not ask him to be a pass-rusher’s decoy with no plan.

xsandos.title: Cover 2 on standard downs
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 and 2nd-and-medium at Seattle, after a 57-yard shot leaked last week
xsandos.why: Two deep, five under takes away the Johnston-style go ball and lets Bolton, coming off 11 tackles, rally to the checkdown.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo: corners sink, safeties stay on top, linebackers fit the run that Seattle will steal from Kansas City’s own tape. Rally and tackle. No freelance deep jump.

xsandos.title: Call the zone blitz, do not narrate last week’s picks
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6, Seattle in the shotgun, offense expecting a soft look after Cover 2
xsandos.why: Show heat, drop a lineman, rush a second-level player — Spagnuolo’s signature as a call for this trip, not an explanation of Cochrane’s interception or Sneed’s forced fumble.
xsandos.coaching: Declare the dropper before the snap. Bolton or a safety can be the rusher. The dropped lineman owns the hot throw. Conner’s pass-rush win last week does not make this card a sack prediction.

coaching.topic: Reid and Bieniemy, points per drive
coaching.detail: 422 yards and 22 points is a finishing problem. The script should be run-first, then defined answers on third down, not more empty volume.
Cover 2 to erase the 57-yard leak, and a zone blitz he calls on purpose. Cochrane, Sneed, and Tranquill already have their credits from the Chargers tape.
An 11-tackle game is the standard for the road. Gilman’s snap share dropped to 49 percent in Week 6, so the sub-package communication has to be explicit.

injuries.note: Arrowhead Addict reports the Chiefs activated his practice window ahead of Week 7 preparation. That is a step, not a declaration he plays at Seattle.

personnel.move: Aiden Fisher to the practice squad
personnel.detail: Arrowhead Pride and Arrowhead Addict report the rookie linebacker, a former Indiana teammate of left tackle Kahlil Benson, is expected to sign. Depth, not a Week 7 starter announcement.

personnel.move: Mecole Hardman to the Colts practice squad
personnel.detail: Arrowhead Pride notes the reunion rumors; Hardman signed in Indianapolis. Justin Watson, separately, was elevated and played one offensive snap and three special-teams snaps against the Chargers.
Arrowhead Addict has him at 42 snaps in Week 6 after a practice-squad call-up, with 1 catch on the touch chart and an interception on a ball intended for him.
From 90 percent of defensive snaps in Week 4 to 49 percent in Week 6, per Arrowhead Addict. A possible secondary shift, not a released player.

strategies: Lead with inside zone to Walker so Seattle’s front has to fit the run before it hunts Mahomes.
Use a boot as a called constraint once that run is respected, with Kelce in the flat.
On third-and-medium, mesh rather than another low-percentage third down after a 3-of-10 game.
Throw the spacing screen to Walker when the rush declares, protecting a quarterback who took 3 hits and 0 sacks.
Start defensive series in Cover 2 so a Johnston-length shot is a rally, not a score.
Dial one zone blitz per series as a Spagnuolo call, with the dropper identified, and keep special teams conservative inside Butker’s made range.
debates: Is 22 points on 422 a sustainable offense, or a five-game disguise the tougher slate will expose?
Should Armstrong’s 42 snaps continue if the production stays at 1 catch?
Does Gilman at 49 percent of the snaps mean a real secondary change or a one-game rotation?
Who do you trust more this week, ESPN FPI at 52.8 percent or DraftKings at Seattle -2.5?
Is Bolton’s franchise mark for 10-tackle games a compliment or a sign the defense is tackling too far downfield?

runOfShow.talkTrack: Five-and-oh, 22-6, 422 yards, and Seattle still laying 2.5. That split is the show.

Walk the scoring order: field goal at Q1 11:20, Walker’s 33-yard touchdown at Q1 7:21 with the extra point missed, Chargers field goals of 23 and 30, Kansas City’s 2-yard touchdown and Butker’s 50 and 30. Team lines: 150 rush, 272 net pass, 30:26. Herbert 22-of-37, 4 sacks, 63.3. Mahomes 23-of-30, 0 sacks, 89.9.

Third-and-10 efficiency at 3-of-10, the missed kicks, the Hart interception, Gillotte’s roughing, Armstrong’s snaps versus his 1 catch. Prior game in Las Vegas stays in its own box: 189 rush, 210 net pass, 24:18.
Inside zone, boot, mesh, screen, Cover 2, and a called zone blitz. Kickoff string is Sun Oct 25, 7:20 PM CT, NBC. FPI 52.8, Seattle -2.5, total 42.5, Polymarket 11.2 and 18.5.
Credit Cochrane, Sneed, and Tranquill by name. No invented score. Look ahead, then stop.
